brief: GS trading-desk daily wrap, 7 Oct 2026. S&P hit a new all-time high (+58bps to 7818, +14% ytd, #28 ATH of 2026) despite macro worries, with momentum/small caps lagging and breadth at its lowest since 2000. Quote of the Day attributes the NDX breakout to three forces: hedge-fund net exposure near a 5-year low, covering of macro hedges, and dollar concentration into Tech/AI, against a backdrop of still-strong AI fundamentals. GS flags upside to semiconductor estimates: after an 11% SOX pullback versus a 4% S&P gain, the setup looks more constructive into earnings, a reversal from GS's cautious 2Q stance. Q3 earnings preview: consensus sees 27% y/y S&P EPS growth, with AI infrastructure spend over 50% of that growth and hyperscaler capex up 116%, even as the median stock's growth decelerates to ~9% from 14% in Q2. GS economists model higher rates subtracting only ~0.2% from 2027 GDP via housing, consumption and capex. Also: Marvell's FY31 targets, a Google-Constellation nuclear deal, Anthropic usage pullbacks at Microsoft/Meta, SpaceX's Nvidia-chip financing push, Apple's smart-home plans, and a hot ISM services prices-paid print.
